shared_elements: coarse pale stone as the carved medium
paired or repeated rounded motifs set in the upper zone
a broad upper element above a plainer, blockier lower body
justification: The clearest correspondence is generic: both are worked in coarse pale stone and place rounded, repeated disc- or loop-like forms in an upper zone above a plainer lower mass, giving each a vaguely top-heavy, T-like profile. Beyond that they diverge completely — A is a volumetric, fully three-dimensional carving of two abutting lobed heads with deep sunken eye-sockets and no narrative content, while B is a flat slab covered in shallow, linear low relief organised into registers with a zigzag band and identifiable animals (quadruped, birds, a snake-like creature), a rendering manner and iconographic programme with no counterpart in A.
